metadata.title: Learn With Mrs. B: My First English Coloring & Activity Masterclass
metadata.subtitle: A 40-Page 5-Phase ESOL Literacy & Technique Activity Book
metadata.author: Mrs. B (Faustine B. Meralus, M.Ed. ESOL)
metadata.target_audience: Pre-K to 2nd Grade, Early English Learners, Bilingual Diaspora Families (Haitian Creole / Spanish / French)
metadata.pedagogical_framework: 5-Phase Recursive Cognitive Loop (SEE -> SAY -> COLOR -> TRACE -> USE)
metadata.technique_framework: Helen Elliston 4-Layer Depth Formula (Base Wash -> Form Midtone -> Crevice Shade -> Specular Pop)
metadata.print_architecture: Amazon KDP Single-Sided Standard with Facing-Page Instructional Guides

front_matter.title: Full Color Front Cover
front_matter.visual_description: Mrs. B smiling in front of sunny tropical classroom with welcome banners, alphabet letters, cute animals, and crayons.

typography.sub: My First English Coloring & Activity Book

elements.description: Mrs. B signature seal and cheering book mascot

front_matter.title: Color Test & Medium Swatch Page
front_matter.description: 54-circle test grid for alcohol markers, crayons, colored pencils, and gel pens to test bleed and blending.

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Mande pitit ou: 'Kijan ou santi ou jodi a?' epi ede l di 'I feel happy' an angle.

technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply light yellow or sky blue base wash with gentle pressure.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Shade the bottom curved contour with orange/navy to create a 3D sphere.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Deepen the knot and bottom shadow with brown/dark blue.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave a clean curved white oval at the top-right for shiny reflection.

pages.title: Welcome to Mrs. B's Class!
pages.objective: Visual vocabulary introduction and emotional labeling.

illustration_brief.foreground: Smiling Mrs. B waving hello holding a welcoming chalkboard.
illustration_brief.midground: Sunny classroom window with alphabet blocks and emotion balloons.
illustration_brief.background: Soft classroom bookshelf and friendly sunshine.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Point to Mrs. B and say: 'Hello Mrs. B!' Ask your child: 'How does she feel?'
pages.activity: Find and color the 3 smiling faces in the classroom.

pages.title: How Do You Feel?
pages.objective: Oral modeling of sentence frames with expressive visual mirrors.

illustration_brief.foreground: 4 large character emotion mirrors (Happy, Sad, Excited, Calm).
illustration_brief.midground: Speech bubbles with bold text frames: 'I feel happy! / I feel excited!'
illustration_brief.background: Classroom carpet with playful star patterns.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Look in a mirror together. Make a happy face, then an excited face. Say the frame together.
pages.activity: Match each emotion word to the smiling or cheering character face.

pages.title: Color the Feeling Balloons
pages.objective: Color discrimination and motor control matching emotional states.

illustration_brief.foreground: Large balloon cluster with emotion expressions on each balloon.
illustration_brief.midground: Ribbons tying the balloons to a friendly park bench.
illustration_brief.technique_integration: Includes 3-step balloon shine swatch box in the footer.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Color the happy balloon yellow and the excited balloon bright orange.
pages.activity: Color the balloons by emotion code. Leave the white shine spot uncolored!

pages.title: Trace and Write Feelings
pages.objective: Orthographic motor practice and letter formation.

elements: Top: Letter formation strokes for uppercase and lowercase Hh, Ss, Ee.
Middle: Primary dotted ruled lines tracing words 'happy', 'sad', 'friend'.
Bottom: Complete the frame: 'I feel [ h _ _ _ y ].'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Guide your child's hand to trace the letters. Sound out each letter as you write.
pages.activity: Trace all dotted letters, then draw a smiley face on the finish star.

pages.title: This Is Me Today!
pages.objective: Creative synthesis and personalized self-expression.

illustration_brief.foreground: Large decorative picture frame labeled 'MY SELF PORTRAIT'.
illustration_brief.bottom: Fill-in-the-blank writing banner: 'My name is _____ and I feel _____ today!'
illustration_brief.background: Celebration ribbons, stars, and party confetti.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Encourage your child to draw their face today. Praise their drawing and read the sentence out loud.
pages.activity: Draw yourself in the frame! Write your name and color your feeling.

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Mande timoun lan montre fanmi l nan foto a epi di: 'This is my mom / papa'.

technique_tutorial.focus: Skin Tone Blending & Soft Fabric Folds
technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply light peach, warm sand, or rich brown base tone over face and arms.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Blend soft terracotta or cocoa in a circular motion on the cheek apples.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add deeper shadow beneath the jawline and along collar seams.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave the forehead and nose tip slightly lighter for natural depth.

pages.title: Meet the Family Portrait Wall
pages.objective: Visual receptive labeling of family members in oval frames.

illustration_brief.foreground: Gallery wall of 6 framed portraits (Mom, Dad, Grandma, Grandpa, Big Sister, Baby).
illustration_brief.midground: Grandma with her hair bun neatly framed inside her oval portrait.
illustration_brief.background: Cozy living room wallpaper and potted flower plant.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Point to each portrait: 'Who is this? This is grandma!'
pages.activity: Color the portrait frames with your favorite bright colors.

pages.title: Dinner with My Family
pages.objective: Oral sentence practice with dialogue prompts.

illustration_brief.foreground: Family seated together around a warm dinner table with plates and food.
illustration_brief.midground: Speech bubble: 'We eat together. I love my family!'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Practice saying: 'This is my family.' Ask who cooks dinner in your home.
pages.activity: Match the name labels at the bottom to each person at the dinner table.

pages.title: Family Love Heart Maze
pages.objective: Path-finding maze and kinesthetic vocabulary matching.

illustration_brief.foreground: Winding garden path connecting sister, brother, and baby to mom's open arms.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Follow the path from the baby to mommy. Say each word as you pass it.
pages.activity: Color the path red and pink to connect the family together.

pages.title: Trace Family Words
pages.objective: Handwriting and spelling reinforcement.

elements: Letter strokes for Mm, Dd, Ff, Bb.
Primary dotted tracing lines for: 'mom', 'dad', 'family', 'love'.
Sentence frame tracing: 'I love my family.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Help your child hold the crayon with a tripod grip. Trace every letter carefully.
pages.activity: Trace the words, then draw a heart next to your favorite word.

pages.title: My Family Tree
pages.objective: Creative production and personal heritage illustration.

illustration_brief.foreground: Large blooming tree with 5 empty photo apples on branches.
illustration_brief.bottom: Banner: 'These are the people I love!'
illustration_brief.background: Green rolling meadow and blue sky.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Draw or write the names of your family members in the apples.
pages.activity: Draw your family in the tree! Color the leaves and apples.

units.title: School & Classroom
units.theme: Classroom Tools, Daily Routine & Polite Requests

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Mande pitit ou: 'Kisa ou pote nan sak lekòl ou?' epi ede l di 'I have a book'.

technique_tutorial.focus: Wood Grain Desks & Cylindrical Pencil Shading
technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Fill desk top with golden tan or light cedar yellow.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Draw subtle wavy wood grain lines with a light brown pencil.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add darker shadows along the desk legs and under the tabletop lip.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave a long clean highlight stripe down the center of the yellow pencil.

pages.title: Welcome to Our Classroom Desk
pages.objective: Visual labeling of everyday school supplies.

illustration_brief.foreground: Student desk with open notebook, pencil holder, and crayon box.
illustration_brief.midground: Open backpack with labeled school supplies popping out.
illustration_brief.background: Chalkboard with alphabet chart and classroom clock.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Find the pencil on the desk. Say: 'I see a yellow pencil.'
pages.activity: Find and color the 5 school objects hidden on the desk.

pages.title: Classroom Sharing & Polite Words
pages.objective: Practicing polite requests and question frames.

illustration_brief.foreground: Two friendly students sitting at a double desk sharing crayons.
illustration_brief.midground: Speech bubbles: 'Please share the blue crayon.' - 'Thank you!'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Role-play with your child: hand them a crayon when they say 'Please give me the crayon.'
pages.activity: Color the sharing friends and trace the word 'PLEASE'.

pages.title: Color by Supply Number
pages.objective: Cognitive number-matching and fine motor coloring.

illustration_brief.foreground: School bus pulling up to school with numbers 1-5 on different parts.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Match the numbers in the legend to color the school bus correctly.
pages.activity: Color the whole scene using the secret number code!

pages.title: Trace School Supplies
pages.objective: Letter formation and spelling for school nouns.

elements: Letter strokes for Bb, Pp, Cc, Dd.
Primary dotted tracing lines for: 'book', 'pen', 'desk', 'school'.
Sentence frame tracing: 'I have a book.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Have your child say the first sound of each word as they trace (/b/ for book).
pages.activity: Trace all words neatly on the lines.

pages.title: Pack My Dream Backpack
pages.objective: Creative synthesis and drawing favorite tools.

illustration_brief.foreground: Large open backpack with big zipper pockets.
illustration_brief.bottom: Sentence starter: 'In my backpack, I have my favorite _____.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: What 3 things would you pack in your backpack? Draw them inside!
pages.activity: Draw your 3 favorite school items inside the backpack and color it.

units.title: Colors & Shapes
units.theme: Descriptive Adjectives, Color Theory & Everyday Geometry

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Montre yon objè nan kay la epi mande: 'Ki koulè sa ye?' (What color is this?).

technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Fill circle with light lemon yellow.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Blend cadmium orange along the bottom-right curve.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add a touch of deep ruby red at the base shadow to make it pop into a 3D sphere.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave a crisp white highlight spot at the top-left.

pages.title: The Magic Shape Town
pages.objective: Visual identification of geometric forms in everyday buildings.

illustration_brief.foreground: Geometric town with square houses, triangle roofs, circle sun, rectangle doors.
illustration_brief.midground: Circle wheels on cars and star flowers along the road.
illustration_brief.background: Fluffy oval clouds over geometric mountains.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Count how many triangles you see in the roof shapes.
pages.activity: Color the triangles orange and the squares blue.

pages.title: Shape & Color Sorting Match
pages.objective: Oral descriptive adjective practice.

illustration_brief.right_column: Real objects: Round Clock, Square Gift Box, Pizza Slice, Star Badge.
illustration_brief.center: Dotted matching lines with sentence frame: 'The pizza is a triangle.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Match each shape to its real object and say: 'The clock is a circle.'
pages.activity: Draw matching lines and color the pairs to match.

pages.title: Stained Glass Color Mosaic
pages.objective: Color mixing and high-contrast line filling.

illustration_brief.foreground: Stained glass butterfly mosaic with geometric pattern wings.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: What happens when yellow and blue touch? They make green!
pages.activity: Fill the stained glass mosaic according to the letter color key.

pages.title: Trace Shapes & Colors
pages.objective: Geometric contour tracing and word handwriting.

elements: Dotted shape outlines: Circle, Square, Triangle, Star.
Primary dotted tracing lines for: 'red', 'blue', 'star', 'circle'.
Sentence frame: 'The star is yellow.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Trace along the dotted lines without lifting the crayon.
pages.activity: Trace all shapes, then color each one with the named color.

pages.title: Build a Shape Robot!
pages.objective: Creative geometric composition and inventive drawing.

illustration_brief.foreground: Grid canvas with shape bank: 3 circles, 4 squares, 2 triangles, 1 star.
illustration_brief.bottom: Sentence: 'My robot has ___ circles and ___ squares.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Use circles for the head and squares for the body. Build your own robot!
pages.activity: Draw your robot using only geometric shapes, then count them!

units.title: Food & Everyday Needs
units.theme: Nutrition, Table Manners, Basic Physical Needs & Preferences

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Lè lè dine rive, mande: 'Èske ou grangou?' epi ankouraje l di 'I am hungry, I like rice'.

technique_tutorial.focus: Glossy Fruit Skin & Translucent Water Glasses
technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply vibrant primary red over the apple.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Shade deep crimson along the bottom base curve.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add dark brown stem indent and green leaf contour.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave a crisp white reflection dot near the top curve to look juicy and shiny.

pages.title: The Fresh Food Market
pages.objective: Visual labeling of healthy fruits, grains, and beverages.

illustration_brief.foreground: Market stand with wooden fruit crates full of apples, bananas, and bread.
illustration_brief.midground: Friendly market vendor offering fresh apples.
illustration_brief.background: Market canopy tent and clear sunny sky.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Point to the banana. Say: 'I see a yellow banana.'
pages.activity: Find and circle all the fruits on the market table.

pages.title: Mealtime Table Talk
pages.objective: Practicing polite request frames and food preferences.

illustration_brief.foreground: Table setting with plate of rice, bread, apple, and glass of water.
illustration_brief.midground: Speech bubbles: 'I like rice!' - 'May I have water, please?'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Practice the question: 'May I have water, please?' with your child before meals.
pages.activity: Color the foods you love to eat and say their English names out loud.

pages.title: Pack the Healthy Lunchbox
pages.objective: Categorization and cognitive sorting between food and drinks.

illustration_brief.foreground: Open bento lunchbox divided into 4 compartments.
illustration_brief.surrounding: Scattered food items: Apple, Banana, Milk Carton, Sandwich, Cookie.
illustration_brief.technique_integration: Includes glossy fruit highlight swatch guide.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Put healthy foods in the lunchbox! Color the fruit red and the milk blue.
pages.activity: Draw matching arrows to pack the lunchbox and color all items.

pages.title: Trace Food Words
pages.objective: Spelling and handwriting reinforcement for basic needs.

elements: Letter formation for Aa, Bb, Ww, Mm.
Primary dotted tracing lines: 'apple', 'bread', 'water', 'milk'.
Sentence frame: 'I like milk.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Trace the letters slowly. Connect the letter sounds to the pictures.
pages.activity: Trace the words and color the matching food icon.

pages.title: My Dream Dinner Menu
pages.objective: Creative synthesis and drawing a personalized healthy meal.

illustration_brief.foreground: Large decorative dinner plate with fork, spoon, and drinking cup.
illustration_brief.bottom: Sentence starter: 'For dinner, I want _____ and _____.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Ask your child: 'If you could eat anything tonight, what would you choose?'
pages.activity: Draw your dream dinner on the plate and write one food word below.

units.title: Animals & Action Words
units.theme: Wildlife, Pets, Movement Verbs & Physical TPR
sentence_frames: I can run like a dog.

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Fè jwèt la: timoun lan kouri tankou yon chyen epi di 'I can run!'.

technique_tutorial.focus: Fluffy Fur Texture & Layered Bird Feathers
technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply golden tan base coat over puppy body.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Add light brown curved shading under belly and neck.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Use quick outward pencil flicks along the tail and ear edges to simulate fluffy fur.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave muzzle and cheek tops bright for a sweet puppy face.

pages.title: Animals in the Meadow
pages.objective: Visual labeling of animals performing distinct natural actions.

illustration_brief.foreground: Playful puppy running through grass and cute kitten watching.
illustration_brief.midground: Bird soaring in the sky and goldfish leaping in the pond.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Find the bird in the sky. Say: 'The bird can fly!'
pages.activity: Find all 4 animals and color the bird blue.

pages.title: Action Verbs Match & Move
pages.objective: Oral TPR practice connecting verbs to movements.
pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Act out each action together! Jump like a frog and say 'I can jump!'
pages.activity: Match each animal to its action verb and act it out.

pages.title: Animal Habitat River Maze
pages.objective: Path navigation matching animals to their homes.

illustration_brief.foreground: Winding nature trails leading to a Bird Nest, Dog House, and Fish Pond.
illustration_brief.technique_integration: Includes puppy fur flicking technique tutorial box.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Help the puppy find the dog house. Color the path green.
pages.activity: Color the path to lead each animal home!

pages.title: Trace Animal Action Words
pages.objective: Action verb spelling and handwriting practice.

elements: Letter strokes for Rr, Jj, Ss, Ff.
Primary dotted tracing lines: 'run', 'jump', 'swim', 'fly'.
Sentence frame: 'The fish can swim.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Sound out each action word: /r/ /u/ /n/ -> run!
pages.activity: Trace all action verbs, then color the running puppy.

pages.title: My Magical Animal Friend
pages.objective: Inventive drawing combining animal features and super-actions.

illustration_brief.foreground: Open meadow canvas with cloud banner: 'My Magical Animal!'.
illustration_brief.bottom: Sentence starter: 'My animal is a _____ and it can _____!'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Imagine an animal with wings or fins! What super power does it have?
pages.activity: Draw your magical animal friend and write its action verb!

units.title: Community & Helpers
units.theme: Neighborhood Navigation, Civic Helpers & Future Aspirations
sentence_frames: I want to be a firefighter.

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Lè nou pase devan yon ponpye oswa doktè, di: 'A doctor helps us feel better' (Doktè a ede nou).

technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply vibrant fire-engine red over the truck body.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Leave bumper and badge crisp white, adding light gray shadow for chrome reflection.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add dark charcoal in tire treads and undercarriage.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Draw yellow starburst light beams radiating from the siren on top.

pages.title: Our Friendly Community Square
pages.objective: Visual identification of civic buildings and neighborhood helpers.

illustration_brief.foreground: Doctor outside hospital, firefighter beside shiny fire truck, teacher outside school.
illustration_brief.midground: Crossing guard helping students across safe crosswalk.
illustration_brief.background: Park with trees and community grocery store.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Find the fire truck! Say: 'The firefighter helps us stay safe.'
pages.activity: Find all 3 community helpers and color their uniforms.

pages.title: Helper Tools Pairing Board
pages.objective: Explaining functions and oral pairing frames.
pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Who uses the fire hose? Connect the firefighter to the hose!
pages.activity: Match each helper to their tool and say the sentence frame.

pages.title: Where Do I Go in Town?
pages.objective: Map navigation and expressing destinations.

illustration_brief.foreground: Town map with wide paved roads leading from Home -> School -> Park -> Store.
illustration_brief.technique_integration: Includes chrome bumper and siren beam shading guide.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Point to the park. Say: 'I go to the park to play!'
pages.activity: Color the path to the school yellow, and the path to the park green.

pages.title: Trace Helper Sentences
pages.objective: Sentence tracing and capital letter practice.

elements: Helper badges (Star, Medical Cross, Fire Emblem).
Primary dotted sentence tracing: 'A doctor helps us.'
Sentence tracing: 'A teacher helps us learn.'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Trace the whole sentence. Put your finger under each word as you read it.
pages.activity: Trace the sentences and color the helper badges.

pages.title: When I Grow Up!
pages.objective: Future self-expression and aspiration drawing.

illustration_brief.foreground: Open uniform silhouette outfit with customizable badges.
illustration_brief.bottom: Sentence banner: 'When I grow up, I want to be a _____!'

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Ask your child: 'Who do you want to be when you grow up?'
pages.activity: Draw yourself in your dream helper uniform and write your job title!

units.title: Review, Mini Story & Celebration
units.theme: Cumulative Synthesis, Story Reading, Milestone Self-Assessment
units.target_vocabulary: Cumulative Review of all 50 target vocabulary words across Units 1-7
sentence_frames: Hello! My name is Mia. I feel happy. I see a bus. I like apples.
I can read! I can write!

creole_bridge.parent_prompt: Felisite pitit ou pou tout liv li fin fè a! Di l: 'Mwen fyè de ou, ou se yon chanpyon!' (I am proud of you!).

technique_tutorial.step_1_base: Apply vibrant sunny yellow base fill over trophy cup.
technique_tutorial.step_2_form: Shade deep golden ochre/bronze on the inner cup curve and base.
technique_tutorial.step_3_crevice: Add dark brown shadows along handle seams.
technique_tutorial.step_4_highlight: Leave vertical white highlight strips down the trophy center for a mirror-shine polish!

pages.title: My Master Word Picture Dictionary
pages.objective: Cumulative vocabulary retrieval and icon labeling.

illustration_brief.foreground: Grid of 14 illustrated icon tiles representing top words from Units 1-7.
illustration_brief.layout: Clean 2x7 tile layout with bold word headers.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Point to each icon and have your child say the word. Check off the words they know!
pages.activity: Color each icon tile as you say its English name.

pages.title: Mia's Big Day (Story Read-Along)
pages.objective: Sequential reading comprehension and oral narrative retelling.

illustration_brief.panel_1: Mia waking up smiling: 'Hello! My name is Mia. I feel happy.'
illustration_brief.panel_2: Mia riding the yellow bus: 'I see a big yellow bus.'
illustration_brief.panel_3: Mia in school with teacher: 'I see my teacher at school.'
illustration_brief.panel_4: Mia eating lunch with friend: 'I like red apples!'
illustration_brief.layout: 4 clean comic panels with large readable text.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Read the story together once. Then have your child point to the panels and tell the story in their own words.
pages.activity: Color the 4 story panels showing Mia's big day at school.

pages.title: What Happened First? Story Sequencing
pages.objective: Story sequencing comprehension and chronological numbering.

panels: Panel A: Mia eating an apple at school lunch.
Panel B: Mia waking up in the morning.
Panel C: Mia getting on the yellow school bus.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: What did Mia do first in the morning? Write number 1 in that box.
pages.activity: Number the story panels 1, 2, 3 in correct order, then color Mia's happy smile.

pages.title: All About Me Story Writer
pages.objective: Independent sentence completion and personal literacy synthesis.
pages.teacher_parent_prompt: Celebrate as your child writes their own mini-book about themselves!
pages.activity: Complete all 4 sentences and draw your victory star.

pages.title: I Can Do It! Celebration Trophy
pages.objective: Celebration of accomplishment and milestone mastery.

illustration_brief.foreground: Giant golden celebration trophy cup surrounded by 4 achievement stars.
illustration_brief.midground: Mrs. B and cheered classroom friends throwing confetti.
illustration_brief.technique_integration: Includes mirror-gold trophy shading guide in the footer.

pages.teacher_parent_prompt: High five! You finished the entire book with Mrs. B! Sign your name on the trophy.
pages.activity: Color the giant trophy gold, check off all 4 stars, and write your name!

back_matter.title: Master 50-Word Vocabulary Checklist
back_matter.description: Alphabetical checklist of all 50 target vocabulary words by unit with 'I Know It!' star checkboxes.

back_matter.title: Parent & Educator Usage Guide
key_principles: Talk Before You Color (Always practice the oral sentence frame first).
Home-Language Bridge (Accept answers in Haitian Creole/Spanish first, validate meaning, then model English).

back_matter.title: About Mrs. B
back_matter.bio_text: Mrs. Faustine B. Meralus (Mrs. B) is a veteran educator with over 25 years of classroom teaching experience in South Florida. A proud Florida Atlantic University alumna (FAU Class of 2001) with a Master's degree specializing in ESOL (English for Speakers of Other Languages), Mrs. B has empowered thousands of children and immigrant families to achieve English literacy, academic confidence, and cultural pride.
